Shared laws, commands and teaching applying to all within the stated audience or conditions. General does not remove covenant, historical, priestly or household limits. Read the existing Transformed, Fulfilled, Unchanged, Everlasting and other classifications alongside each entry.

Some source records still need their audience resolved. These are explicitly marked audience review pending; their provisional filing here is not a claim that they apply universally. Passage groups may contain both shared teaching and personal directions.

General · Personal · Instructions overview

3,869 study records in this view. Entries can overlap; this is not a count of distinct biblical commands. Ordered by the first source book, chapter and verse.

The source wording follows the Saints Greek-English text: the Septuagint for the Old Testament and the Greek New Testament. Headings and application notes are study summaries. Preserve the passage’s speaker, audience, conditions and grammatical form. Source alignment checked 6 November 2026; independent critical-Greek review remains in progress.

S060 · Restoring property obtained dishonestly

Source wording · Saints Greek-English

This is the cited study context; the record does not identify a separate primary command passage.

5:20 And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying,

5:21 If a soul sins, and utterly disregards the commandments of the Lord, and deals falsely with his neighbour concerning a deposit, or a partnership, or robbery, or any wrong which he has done unto his neighbour,

5:22 or finds a lost thing and deals falsely concerning it, and swears unjustly concerning any of all the things which a man may do so as to sin therein,

5:23 then it shall be, when he has sinned and incurred guilt, that he shall return the plunder which he seized, or that which he obtained by wrong, or the deposit which was entrusted unto him, or the lost thing which he found,

5:24 concerning every matter about which he swore unjustly. And he shall repay the principal, and add a fifth part unto it; he shall repay it unto the one to whom it belongs, on the day when he is convicted.

5:25 And for his offence he shall bring unto the Lord an unblemished ram from the flock, of a value corresponding to the offence which he has committed against Him.

5:26 And the priest shall make atonement for him before the Lord, and he shall be forgiven concerning any of all the things which he has done and wherein he has offended Him.

Leviticus 5:20–26

Audience: Shared instruction or study teaching. Read the original audience, conditions and existing classification before applying it.

Classification: Study context · Topical study

Topic: Human life, injury and care for neighbours

Original scope: Text and setting: Restitution and offering law

Connection to Christ: The fulfillment mark concerns the offering within the former sacrificial order, not the erasure of responsibility for stolen property. Christian response today: Stop the dishonesty and make amends; distinguish restitution from attempting to add another atoning sacrifice.
